summary: Renate Syed is an Indologist who studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1974–1982) for her Doktorgrad der Philosophie under supervisor Dieter Schlingloff and teachers Friedrich Wilhelm and Gritli von Mitterwallner.
Renda Zheng worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Kaizhi in 1969, Shengfa in 1970, and Kaitong from 1971 to 1972.
René Gothóni is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Helsinki (~1970–1982). He subsequently held a post at the University of Helsinki from ~1975 to 2014.

Richard A. Hutch works in religious studies. He studied at Gettysburg College (~1963–1967), Yale Divinity School (~1967–1970), and the University of Chicago (~1970–1974), later holding posts at Southern Illinois University (~1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978).
Richard Baker works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1954–1958) and under traditional teacher Shunryu Suzuki (~1961–1971), whom he later succeeded.
Richard Barron is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and the 3rd Jamgön Kongtrul.
Richard Bowring is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He completed his education at Blundell's School (~1960–1965) and Downing College (~1965–1973).

Richard Carnac Temple worked in Indology and history/archaeology. After studying at Harrow School (~1863–1867) and Trinity Hall (~1868–1871), he served in the Bengal Staff Corps (~1883–1891), the Indian Staff Corps (~1897–1904), and edited The Indian Antiquary (1901).

Richard D. Mann specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University (~1997–2003) under doctoral supervisor Phyllis Granoff and committee members Koichi Shinohara, Alan Mendelson, Gretchen Ulmholtz, and David Kinsley.

Richard D. McBride II works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. at UCLA (~1994–2001) and held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (~2002–2004) and Dongguk University.

Richard F. Nance is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1996–2004) and served as Assistant Professor of South Asian Buddhism at Indiana University (~2005–2012).
Richard Fick was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Kiel from ~1885 to 1888. He later held a post at the University of Göttingen from ~1921 to 1932.

Richard Foltz works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Utah (~1985–1989) and Harvard (~1991–1996), later holding posts at the University of Florida (~2000–2006) and Concordia University (2005).
Richard Fritzsche was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus from ~1872 to 1876. He later held a post as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg.

Richard Gombrich is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his D.Phil. at Oxford (~1963–1970) under Robert Charles Zaehner. He served as Boden Professor at Oxford (1965–2004) and Balliol College (1976), and General Editor at Clay Sanskrit Library (~2004–2008).

Richard Hugh Robinson worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Alberta, SOAS, and the University of London under Arthur Waley and David Friedman, later holding posts at the University of Toronto (1954) and University of Wisconsin-Madison (1961–1971).

Richard Hughes Seager is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD ~1987), later serving as Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College (~1994).
Richard J. Smith is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of California, Davis (~1963–1972) and held a post at Rice University from ~1973 to 2018.

Richard Jay Kohn was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under traditional teacher Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa by 1988.

Richard K. Payne works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology, having studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He has held posts at the University of Chicago, Graduate Theological Union, and as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1994).
